bugs.title: Project/Planner context can unexpectedly return to Home
evidence: ROOT-CAUSED (wave 3, investigation agent): exhaustively grepped tsf/ui/src for any React-side redirect/navigate('/')/error-boundary fallback that could cause this -- none found. The real cause lives entirely outside the React SPA, in the WebView2 desktop launcher (launcher/Launch-TSF.ps1 + launcher/first-run-setup.html): when the launcher's health/connectivity check trips its recovery branch (e.g. a transient backend hiccup while an operator is deep in a Project/Planner view), it unconditionally navigates the WebView2 control to the first-run recovery guide page with no memory of where the operator was -- so once the guide's own readiness check passes, it always lands back on the app's bare root, discarding the real in-app route.

FIXED: the recovery-navigation branch in Launch-TSF.ps1 now captures $webView.Source (skipped if it's a file:// URL, i.e. already on a guide/error page) into a $returnUrl before navigating to the guide, and appends it as a ?return=<url-encoded> query param on the guide URL. first-run-setup.html's checkReady() now reads ?return= (validated to actually start with the real TSF_URL origin before being trusted, else falls back to the bare TSF_URL exactly as before) and navigates there once ready, instead of always to the bare root.

Validated via static syntax checking only: [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile(...) on Launch-TSF.ps1 (SYNTAX OK) and Node's vm.Script on the extracted <script> content of first-run-setup.html (SCRIPT SYNTAX OK). DISCLOSED GAP: no live functional test exists or was run -- this environment has no WebView2 test harness, and the failure mode itself (a live desktop launcher recovery flow) is not reproducible via the server/UI test suites in tsf/. Manual verification (trigger a real recovery-guide navigation from inside a deep Project/Planner route, confirm it returns to that exact route once ready) is a required real-project check before adoption, not yet performed.

No server or UI test suite touches this file (it's outside both npm test's and the UI's node --experimental-strip-types --test scope) -- typecheck/build/full suite results for this bug are 'not applicable, no automated coverage possible in this environment', not silently omitted.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context) found ONE real defect: resolveReturnUrl()'s validation was raw.startsWith(TSF_URL) -- a plain string-prefix check, NOT a real origin boundary. Live-demonstrated bypasses: 'http://127.0.0.1:4610.evil.com/redirect'.startsWith('http://127.0.0.1:4610') === true, and 'http://127.0.0.1:46100/evil'.startsWith(...) === true -- either would have let a malicious ?return= value navigate the trusted embedded WebView2 off-origin, directly contradicting the code's own comment claiming a same-origin check. Verifier's own severity disclosure: not confirmed exploitable through any live path in this codebase today (the only current writer of ?return= is Launch-TSF.ps1 reading the WebView2's own trusted live .Source), but a real, latent correctness/defense-in-depth gap, not a style nitpick.

FIXED: resolveReturnUrl() now compares new URL(raw, TSF_URL).origin === new URL(TSF_URL).origin -- a real parsed-origin (scheme+host+port) check instead of a string prefix. Re-verified live against the verifier's own exact repro cases plus additional bypass patterns (protocol-relative //evil.com/x, userinfo-trick http://127.0.0.1:4610@evil.com/x): all correctly rejected; the original legitimate case (a same-origin deep link carrying its own ?tab=/&runId=/#fragment) still round-trips correctly. Re-checked SCRIPT SYNTAX OK via the same Node vm.Script extraction used originally.

The verifier's own PowerShell-side checks (Launch-TSF.ps1's $webView.Source -and -not $webView.Source.IsFile short-circuiting safely on a null Source; EscapeDataString/URLSearchParams round-trip fidelity for a return URL containing its own query params) both passed live repro -- no defect found there, no change made to Launch-TSF.ps1 this round.

SECOND INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context, re-checking the round-1 fix itself): NOT READY -- found a new, more severe real bypass rooted in a base-URL mismatch between where raw is VALIDATED and where it is later USED. resolveReturnUrl() validates raw by resolving it against the hardcoded TSF_URL, but then returns the UNRESOLVED raw string -- and this script can itself be loaded from a file:// document (Launch-TSF.ps1 navigates here via a local file path), so location.href = RETURN_URL later re-resolves that SAME raw string against a file:// base instead. Live-demonstrated: new URL('http:evil.com', 'http://127.0.0.1:4610').origin reads as the safe origin (validation passes), but new URL('http:evil.com', 'file:///.../first-run-setup.html').href resolves to 'http://evil.com/' -- a scheme-relative value with no '//' authority passes validation yet navigates to an EXACT evil.com origin, not just a lookalike -- arguably worse than the original two bypasses. Verifier also positively confirmed (not just this one gap): userinfo tricks, IPv6/decimal/octal host variants, javascript:/data: schemes (opaque origin, correctly rejected), and whitespace/control-char prefixes were all already handled correctly by the round-1 fix -- only the scheme-relative/base-mismatch class was the real remaining gap.

FIXED (round 2): resolveReturnUrl() now returns the RESOLVED absolute href (new URL(raw, TSF_URL).href) instead of the raw string, so the exact value validated is byte-for-byte the exact value later navigated to -- no second resolution against a different (file://) base can ever happen again. Re-verified live against the verifier's exact repro (http:evil.com now correctly resolves to the safe origin as http://127.0.0.1:4610/evil.com, a harmless path on the real origin, not a redirect) plus every previously-tested case (legit deep link with query+fragment, both original lookalike bypasses, protocol-relative, userinfo, javascript: scheme, malformed, missing) -- all still correct. Re-checked SCRIPT SYNTAX OK.

THIRD INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context): READY, no defect found. Confirmed base-independence is real per the WHATWG URL Standard (an absolute-URL string ignores any base when parsed -- verified live with three different bases, file://, a hostile http:// origin, and none, all producing the identical result), so location.href = RETURN_URL can never be reinterpreted against the file:// document base again. Re-tried every bypass from both prior rounds plus new ones (backslash tricks, doubly-encoded values, IDN/punycode homographs, whitespace/null-byte prefixes, a raw file:// value, fragment/query-based lookalikes) -- all correctly rejected; the two genuinely-same-origin userinfo cases correctly still resolve either way. Confirmed the real production round-trip (Launch-TSF.ps1's EscapeDataString(AbsoluteUri) -> URLSearchParams.get -> resolveReturnUrl) reproduces a functionally equivalent URL, with the only normalization being an authority-only URL gaining a trailing slash (functionally identical for HTTP, and doesn't arise from real .NET AbsoluteUri values anyway, which already normalize this). SCRIPT SYNTAX OK re-confirmed. Three verification rounds total for this file (2 found real defects and were fixed; the 3rd found nothing) -- code-level closure now matches this ledger's own bar (see BUG-08's identical 3-round pattern).

REMAINING DISCLOSED GAP, unaffected by the above: no live WebView2 functional test has ever been run in this environment (none exists) -- every round of verification here is static syntax + URL-parsing-semantics analysis, never an actual rendered recovery-guide navigation. A real, live manual check (trigger the launcher's recovery path from inside a deep Project/Planner route on a real machine, confirm it returns to that exact route) remains a required real-project validation step before final adoption, exactly as this mission's own acceptance bar requires.

bugs.title: Project Work Set/selection behavior across tabs is confusing
evidence: ROOT-CAUSED (wave 3, investigation agent, three distinct real defects, not one): (1) the real cascade -- domain/portfolio.mjs's setActiveFleet already enforces that removing Active Fleet membership also removes Work Set membership (Work Set is a real subset of Active Fleet), but this was never surfaced anywhere a bulk removal actually happens -- an operator bulk-removing projects from Active Fleet had no way to know Work Set membership silently went with it. (2) ProjectCard.tsx already had project.activeFleet/project.workSet on its own data model but never rendered either, so the Projects grid -- the primary place an operator selects/acts on projects -- showed no membership state at all, only the detail page did. (3) inconsistent terminology/explanation: the real explanatory copy for Active Fleet/Work Set existed only in prose on MembershipPanel.tsx (single-project detail page); BulkActionBar.tsx, the primary bulk-action surface, showed only the bare words with none of it, and the same 'selected' checkbox pattern silently means different things across ProjectsPage.tsx (all Known Projects) vs FleetPage.tsx (Active Fleet only).

FIXED: ui/src/lib/membership-tier-copy.ts (new) -- single source of truth for ACTIVE_FLEET_EXPLANATION/WORK_SET_EXPLANATION/ACTIVE_FLEET_REMOVAL_CASCADE_NOTE plus a pure, tested cascadedFromWorkSet(applied, workSetBefore) helper, so the copy and the cascade-detection arithmetic can never read differently on one surface than another and are never left untested inside a component. MembershipPanel.tsx now imports the shared constants instead of its own inline strings. BulkActionBar.tsx: added a required workSetBefore prop (the real pre-action Work Set membership, threaded from ProjectsPage.tsx's own portfolio.workSet), its membership() action now honestly reports the real cascade via cascadedFromWorkSet when a bulk Active-Fleet removal actually drops Work Set membership too, and both dropdown menus now show the shared explanation text (plus the cascade note under Active Fleet). ProjectCard.tsx now renders conditional Fleet/Work Set badges (shown only when true, to keep the common non-member case uncluttered) with tooltips using the same shared copy.

4 new tests (membership-tier-copy.test.ts) cover cascadedFromWorkSet directly: a removed+previously-in-Work-Set project is reported, a removed-but-never-in-Work-Set project is not, a Work-Set project the server actually skipped (not in applied) is correctly not reported (applied is the real source of truth, not the pre-action selection), and the empty-input case. tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean (1917 modules), 82/82 ui tests pass (up from 78, confirming the 4 new tests actually ran).

Not yet done: verified by direct re-read that FleetPage.tsx does NOT share BulkActionBar -- it has its own separate, unlabeled 'selected' checkbox that only ever iterates portfolio.workSet (already-Work-Set projects, for scheduling/Start Overnight Fleet selection) with no membership semantics at all, while ProjectsPage.tsx's checkbox iterates all portfolio.knownProjects and drives real Active-Fleet/Work-Set membership changes via BulkActionBar -- confirming the third defect (same checkbox pattern, two unrelated meanings) is real but NOT yet fixed. A distinct page-level label clarifying what each page's selection actually does is disclosed here as remaining, deliberately-deferred polish, not silently dropped.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context) found ONE real, reproducible race defect: BulkActionBar.tsx's run() calls onChanged() (ProjectsPage's reload(), which only bumps a tick and returns immediately -- use-api.ts's reload never awaits the actual portfolio refetch) and then clears busy in its own finally, re-enabling every action button well before the refetch resolves and the workSetBefore prop actually updates. Concrete repro the verifier traced: select P1/P2 (Active Fleet, not Work Set) -> Add to Work Set (server applies it; busy clears almost immediately, before reload's fetch lands) -> before that refetch resolves, Remove from Active Fleet on the same selection -> server-side this genuinely cascades P1/P2 out of Work Set too (they were just added) -> but membership()'s cascadedFromWorkSet(result.applied, workSetBefore) reads the STALE pre-step-1 workSetBefore (not yet listing P1/P2), so it silently reports NO cascade even though one really happened -- directly contradicting the fix's own stated purpose ('honestly report the real cascade'). Untested by the 82/82 passing suite since no BulkActionBar.tsx component test exists (only the pure cascadedFromWorkSet helper is unit-tested).

FIXED: BulkActionBar now takes a required refreshing: boolean prop (ProjectsPage passes its own real portfolio loading flag) and disables every action button while it's true, in addition to the existing busy check. use-api.ts's loading becomes true for the FULL duration of any reload (including a background one) and clears in the exact same state update that delivers the fresh portfolio/workSetBefore -- so gating new actions on !refreshing guarantees the next action can only start once workSetBefore is genuinely current, closing the race without needing to make onChanged itself awaitable (a broader change touching every useApi caller, out of proportion to this one bug). tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean (1917 modules), 82/82 ui tests still pass (fix is UI-wiring-only, no new pure-logic surface to unit test beyond the existing cascadedFromWorkSet coverage).

SECOND INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context, re-checking the fix itself): READY, no blocking defect. Traced use-api.ts's load()/effect-cleanup interaction directly: a second reload() fired while one is already in flight correctly runs the PRIOR effect's cleanup (cancelled=true) before the new one starts, so a superseded fetch's .then/.finally can never clear loading early or overwrite fresh data with stale data; a thrown fetch always still clears loading via .finally() (no stuck-disabled-forever case). Two non-blocking notes disclosed by the verifier, not defects: (1) refreshing disables ALL BulkActionBar actions (including ones with no workSetBefore dependency, e.g. Analyze/Scan Health/Prepare for Work) during ANY portfolio reload anywhere on the page, broader than strictly required but never leaves genuinely stale data clickable, judged an acceptable tradeoff; (2) a theoretical single-frame window inherent to any useEffect-driven refetch (setTick/setBusy commit vs. the effect's own later setLoading(true)) is far smaller than the unbounded-network-duration race this fix closes, not practically exploitable. tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean, 82/82 ui tests pass, 3/3 golden-path tests pass (test/golden-path-operator-flow.test.mjs).

Status intentionally kept at VERIFYING, not READY_FOR_ADOPTION, despite the code fixes above being independently verified clean: the cascade-visibility fix and the workSetBefore staleness race are both genuinely closed, but this bug's OWN root-cause investigation identified a third real defect (FleetPage.tsx's separate, differently-scoped 'selected' checkbox -- see the 'Not yet done' evidence entry above) that remains deliberately unfixed. Marking the whole bug READY_FOR_ADOPTION while a disclosed root cause is still open would be exactly the status inflation this mission was explicitly told to avoid (see BUG-08's own ledger-correction precedent). Split or close the FleetPage.tsx gap in a following wave before this entry can honestly move to READY_FOR_ADOPTION.

bugs.title: Repair/run state becomes unclear after navigating away
evidence: Prior stalled run keep-going-tsf-orca-1787691592122 targeted this same bug ('Repair Health navigation/state bug') and left unverified, uncommitted changes to ProjectHealthRepairCard.tsx/HealthRepairCenterPage.tsx and a new tsf/ui/src/lib/health-repair-activity.ts(+test) in worktree command-tsf-orca-1788395222325 -- not reused without independent reproduction/review. Its own independent verification pass (2026-09-03T00:53:25Z) found this criterion still unsatisfied.
Directly related to the P0 canonical-state theme, not just a UI polish item -- tracked P0 here.

ROOT-CAUSED (2026-09-03, read-only investigation, wave 2): Health Repair (healthRepairBaseline/Repair/PrepareMission/Selected -- health-repair-http-routes.mjs, health-repair.mjs) is a DISTINCT feature from Prepare for Work (prepare-for-work-http-routes.mjs/prepare-for-work-store.mjs/domain/prepare-for-work-operation.mjs) with a materially weaker durability guarantee -- do not conflate them. Prepare for Work already has a real durable operationId/phase/status record (opState.prepareForWorkOperations) with GET routes to list/poll it without a remembered id (already tested, confirmed in wave 1) -- Health Repair has NONE of this (confirmed by grep: zero 'operationId' occurrences anywhere in health-repair*.mjs). Each Health Repair action is one long-lived synchronous HTTP request (baseline checks alone can run ~2min/category sequentially per health-repair.mjs's own TSF_HEALTH_REPAIR_TIMEOUT_MS default; repair-selected loops sequentially over every selected project x every cause) tracked ONLY in the calling React component's own useState (ProjectHealthRepairCard.tsx/HealthRepairCenterPage.tsx) -- no AbortController, so navigating away neither cancels the real server-side work nor preserves any way to see its outcome; the response is delivered to an already-unmounted component and silently dropped. Reproduction: start 'Repair selected' or 'Run baseline check' on a project with a slow discovered test/build/lint command, navigate to Home before it finishes, then return to Health Repair Center -- the rescan shows either a stale pre-repair diagnosis with no in-progress indicator (if the real work is still running) or the new diagnosis with zero record a repair action ever ran (if it already finished) -- no operationId, no phase, no history anywhere.

The prior stalled run's own unverified attempt (health-repair-activity.ts, other worktree) does not actually close this either -- its backing store is a module-level in-memory JS Map, not server-persisted -- survives a component remount within the same page session but not a real process restart, and reconciles against no genuine server-side durable id.

SCOPING DECISION: closing this honestly requires a genuine new durable-operation backend design for Health Repair (its own persisted operationId/phase/status record, comparable in shape to prepareForWorkOperations but a real design decision whether to reuse or build separately -- the investigation explicitly flags this as 'a real design decision, not a given', not a bounded UI-only wiring fix like most of this mission's other bugs). Deliberately NOT attempted within wave 2 alongside BUG-15/persistent-visibility -- rushing a new durable-operation subsystem without its own design/review pass risks the exact kind of half-built, later-distrusted state this mission exists to clean up. Deferred to its own dedicated following wave, disclosed here with full root-cause and reproduction evidence so that wave can start from ground truth rather than re-investigating.

IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-03, wave 3): chose 'build separately' from the two options the scoping decision named -- a new, structurally-mirrored-but-independent durable-operation system (domain/health-repair-operation.mjs, server/health-repair-store.mjs, both closely modeled on prepare-for-work-operation.mjs/prepare-for-work-store.mjs, sharing the same lock file for cross-store write safety) rather than generalizing the already-adopted Prepare for Work code, to keep zero blast radius on that working, independently-reviewed feature. server/health-repair-http-routes.mjs rewritten: baseline/repair/repair-selected (the genuinely slow, async actions) now create a durable operation and return 202 immediately; the real work (unchanged functions/order/bulk-safety posture) runs detached, persisting phase/result per project. /scan and /prepare-mission stay direct synchronous responses (confirmed fast/no I/O -- wrapping them would add ceremony with no benefit). Startup recovery wired into http-server.mjs, mirroring Prepare for Work's own. Lifecycle: QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/NEEDS_YOU (NEEDS_YOU substitutes for the mission driver's suggested 'cancelled' -- no real cancel primitive exists anywhere in health-repair.mjs, so NEEDS_YOU, an already-established real TIM_REQUIRED-driven halt, is used instead of fabricating one). UI: ui/src/lib/health-repair-polling.ts (new, mirrors prepare-for-work-polling.ts) + ui/src/lib/api.ts rewired -- ProjectHealthRepairCard.tsx/HealthRepairCenterPage.tsx need no changes to their public call shape, only how api.ts fulfills it.

Two real golden-path proofs added (test/http-health-repair.test.mjs): 'BUG-05 FRONTEND DISCONNECT' (never polls again after starting an operation -- reads the store directly and confirms the real work completed server-side anyway) and 'BUG-05 RECOVERY' (plants a RUNNING-but-orphaned operation, calls the real startup-recovery function, confirms reacquisition under the same id and a real terminal state). Both mirror Prepare for Work's own already-adopted equivalents exactly.

A real bug caught mid-implementation by my own trace-through (not the independent verifier): the rewrite initially dropped the per-project loop's try/catch (previously inline in the synchronous /repair-selected route, protecting 'one project's failure never stops another's') and separately dropped the causesBefore field from /repair's result -- both fixed before the first independent-verification pass, with the exact adversarial test ('a real exception on one project neither loses an earlier project's completed repair nor skips a later project') re-run to confirm.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context) found ONE real, reproducible defect: ProjectHealthRepairCard.tsx's repair() unconditionally accessed result.repairResult.reason on an ok:false result -- but when the background runner itself throws (the exact real exception path the adversarial test above exercises), the settled result is honestly {ok:false, error} with NO repairResult field at all, so this threw a TypeError that got masked into a useless generic 'Repair failed.' message, discarding the real, specific server-provided error text. Fixed: RepairActionResult's fields (repairResult/causesBefore/causesAfter/readyForWork) made honestly optional to match the real reachable shape; repair() now checks result.error first. 1 new regression test added reproducing the exact exception-shaped result. Everything else the verifier checked (locking/concurrency, the try/catch fix, response-shape parity for every other field, both golden-path proofs, full test suites -- 85/85 across the health-repair/prepare-for-work test files, 69/69 ui tests at that point) passed clean.

9/9 health-repair-operation domain tests, 13/13 http-health-repair tests (11 original adversarial security tests re-verified intact + 2 new golden-path proofs), 9/9 health-repair-polling ui tests (incl. the verifier-found regression), tsc -b --noEmit clean, vite build clean, zero regressions across the full server (1005/1007, 1 known pre-existing flake) and ui (78/78) suites.
Second independent-verification pass on the fix itself recommended -- see status once it lands.

bugs.title: New mission creation vs dispatching work into an existing mission is unclear
evidence: ROOT-CAUSED: chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's planAndDispatchFromChat already computed a real freshlyCreated boolean (from ensureActiveRun -- whether it started a brand-new Keep Going run or reused an already-ACTIVE one) but silently discarded it before returning, so http-server.mjs's dispatchedText always said the same generic 'Dispatched...' regardless of which actually happened -- an operator dispatching via chat/command had no way to tell 'this started a new mission' from 'this added to a mission already running'.

FIXED: planAndDispatchFromChat now returns freshlyCreated (destructured, not discarded); dispatchOneProject (fleet-wide command dispatch) threads the same real field through into its own detail text and result. http-server.mjs's dispatchedText now branches on the real value: 'Started a new mission for **X**' vs 'Added to the mission already running for **X**' -- never a fabricated distinction, always the real ensureActiveRun outcome. command-responder.mjs's multi-project summary line simplified to drop a redundant double 'dispatched' now that dispatch.detail itself already states the real freshlyCreated phrasing.

2 new assertions (chat-dispatch-bridge.test.mjs: freshlyCreated===true on a fresh dispatch, ===false on reuse of an existing ACTIVE run) plus 2 existing tests fixed after discovering their old case-sensitive /Dispatched/ regex broke against the new lowercase mid-sentence phrasing (http-chat-dispatch.test.mjs, http-command.test.mjs -> /Started a new mission.*dispatched/s). All 69 relevant tests (chat-dispatch-bridge, http-chat-dispatch, http-command, http-chat-live, chat-responder, command-responder) pass. Full server suite re-run after this change: 1005/1007 pass, the 2 known pre-existing Windows-contention flakes (health-repair-io.test.mjs's timeout-kill test, keep-going-autonomy-proof.test.mjs) both reconfirmed passing in isolation, 1 skipped -- no regression from this change.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (separate agent context): READY, no defects found. Traced ensureActiveRun's every real branch (existing run of any state -> false; no run, start() succeeds -> true; race loser catches TSF_RUN_ALREADY_ACTIVE and re-reads -> false) and confirmed planAndDispatchFromChat already filters out non-ACTIVE states before/after ensureActiveRun, so freshlyCreated can never leak into an ok:true response for a state it doesn't actually describe. dispatchOneProject/http-server.mjs/command-responder.mjs's template strings/branching all checked -- no typos, no stale booleans, no double-'dispatched:' prefix. 48/48 targeted tests (chat-dispatch-bridge, http-chat-dispatch, http-command, keep-going-dispatch-loop) pass; full suite 1006/1008 pass (the one known pre-existing flake, reconfirmed passing in isolation).

bugs.title: Orca/Windows notifications expose raw internal run IDs and are noisy
evidence: ROOT-CAUSED: this bug is genuinely hybrid, not a single defect. TSF-owned half: keep-going-dispatch-loop.mjs's createOrchestrationTask call never populated displayName (only spec/run/taskTitle), so any Orca-core surface that renders a task's displayName (title templates, terminal titles, OS notifications) had nothing but the bare internal work-item id to fall back to. Orca-core half: the actual raw-ID notification/terminal-title rendering itself (title templates, worktreeLabel, terminalTitle) lives entirely in src/main/ipc/notifications.ts, notification-options.ts, src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts, src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/use-notification-dispatch.ts -- all Orca core, explicitly outside this mission's write authority per HQ.md's boundary (confirmed by direct investigation, not assumed).

FIXED (TSF-owned half only): keep-going-dispatch-loop.mjs now also passes displayName: `${projectId}: ${item.scope.slice(0, 3).join(', ')}` -- composed only from real, already-available facts (the real projectId + the real file scope already on the work item), never a fabricated 'friendly project name' that doesn't exist anywhere in the domain. This gives Orca-core's own notification/title rendering a real human-readable value to use instead of the bare work-item id, without this mission touching Orca-core itself.

1 new regression test (keep-going-dispatch-loop.test.mjs): 'a real dispatch supplies a human-readable displayName -- project id + real file scope, never just the bare work-item id', asserting the exact composed string. All 21 tests in this file pass.

NOT FIXED, explicitly disclosed rather than silently dropped: the Orca-core half (actual notification noise/formatting/raw-ID display in the OS notification itself) is untouched -- out of this mission's write authority. bugs.title: RESCOPED 2026-09-03 (ledger correction, see BUG-08 vs BUG-17 note below): negated consequential language (e.g. "do not merge/push/deploy") must classify as a restriction, never a request -- classification correctness only. The original title's second half ("...may fail to consume explicit approval once") is now BUG-17 -- a distinct, still-REPORTED, not-yet-started mechanism. This entry's READY_FOR_ADOPTION applies ONLY to the classification-correctness scope below, never to approval-consumption, which does not exist and was never implemented under this id.
evidence: LEDGER CORRECTION (2026-09-03, prompted by an explicit operator check): this bug's original title bundled two materially different things -- (a) negated language must classify as a restriction (a pure classification-correctness question, real bugs found/fixed/verified below) and (b) a scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism (a distinct, unbuilt feature -- see the 'SCOPING DECISION' entry below, which was already honest about it being deferred and not started). Marking the WHOLE bug READY_FOR_ADOPTION was status inflation given ACCEPT-07's acceptance criterion ('...consumes scoped approval once') was never satisfied. Split: this id now covers ONLY (a), genuinely done and 3x independently verified below; (b) is split out to BUG-17, status REPORTED, not started. ACCEPT-07 stays REPORTED until BUG-17 lands too -- see its own entry in the acceptance[] array below.

Independent read-only investigation (separate agent context) traced the actual regex logic live against real messages: every example the ledger's own evidence named ("do not merge this", "please do not push to production", a negation-plus-unrelated-directive combined message) already classified correctly -- the adversarial-hardened comma/"but"/em-dash clause-splitting genuinely works.

But it found a REAL, reproducible gap in the same class: splitIntoClauses (chat-responder.mjs) never treated a bare "and" (no comma) as a clause boundary, so a negation and a genuine, separate directive joined only by "and" stayed one clause and the negation laundered the directive through as non-TIM_REQUIRED. Live-reproduced: 'do not deploy this and push it now' -> AUTO_DECIDE (wrong); 'please do not deploy and go ahead and merge this' -> RECOMMEND_AND_PROCEED (wrong). Reproduces identically on the Command surface (command-responder.mjs reuses the same functions unmodified).

Fix: added \band\b to the same clause-boundary normalization regex, exactly mirroring the existing "but"/comma/em-dash precedent. Both repro cases now correctly TIM_REQUIRED; verified live and via 4 new regression tests (chat-responder.test.mjs) plus the full existing 25-case suite unchanged (34/34 total across chat+command responder tests).

Investigation also found: there is NO approval-consumption mechanism anywhere in the codebase (grepped server/domain for approve/consume/grant/scope) -- every chat/command turn is independently reclassified from the bare current message with zero conversational memory. Practically this makes TIM_REQUIRED for push/merge/deploy/publish/credentials/money/adopt an unconditional refusal via chat today: restating with the keyword re-triggers TIM_REQUIRED every time, and chat is structurally zero-tool (--tools "") plus chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's generated plans hard-forbid this action class regardless -- so there is currently no execution path for this class of action via chat at all, whatever the approval state. respondTimRequired()'s old text falsely promised a 'tell me explicitly to proceed and I'll surface exactly what would change... before anything happens' preview flow that doesn't exist anywhere -- fixed to honestly say chat cannot act on it and point to the real surface (Adoption tab / terminal).

SCOPING DECISION: a genuine scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism (the user's fuller ask: 'consumed once', 'must not leak to another operation/project/action class') is real product value but is itself a security-sensitive, non-trivial feature (new persisted state, new UI, cross-turn tracking) -- deliberately deferred to a following bounded wave rather than rushed in alongside this wave's other 5 bugs, per the mission driver's own explicit allowance ('this stabilization wave or the immediately following bounded wave'). What's fixed now (the real negation gap, and the honesty fix removing the false promise/refusal-loop) is real, verified, and independently investigated; the deferred piece is disclosed here, not silently dropped.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (first pass) found the \band\b fix itself introduced a NEW real false-negative regression: when 'and'-splitting isolates an informal, subject-less future-tense fragment as its own clause (e.g. '...and will deploy after that', '...and should merge soon'), that clause starts with a bare inquiry-opener word ('will'/'should') purely by grammatical coincidence -- INQUIRY_OPENERS' bare-opener alternative wrongly read it as a question with no '?' anywhere. Live-reproduced: 'run the tests and will deploy after that' -> AUTO_DECIDE (wrong, was TIM_REQUIRED-worthy).

Fixed: split INQUIRY_OPENERS into BARE_OPENER (bare opener word) and TELL_ME_WHETHER (the 'tell me...whether' shape, unconditional). BARE_OPENER now additionally requires the clause's own SENTENCE to contain a real '?' -- TELL_ME_WHETHER stays unconditional since it's unambiguously interrogative regardless of punctuation. Verified against both the new regression cases (now correctly TIM_REQUIRED) and every prior passing case (unchanged) live before adding tests. 2 new regression tests added (31/31 chat-responder tests pass).

Second independent-verification pass confirmed both the negation-gap fix and its own found BARE_OPENER regression are correct (READY) via ~20 adversarial phrasings the implementer never tried, plus its own sentence-vs-clause scoping check. It also found a THIRD real, pre-existing gap (unrelated to the 'and' fix, surfaced incidentally while re-checking it): PROHIBITION_MARKERS' bare 'not'/'no' match had no idiom awareness, so 'whether ... or not'/'no matter' (meaning 'regardless') wrongly read as real negations -- 'deploy it whether tim likes it or not' classified AUTO_DECIDE instead of TIM_REQUIRED.

Fixed: IDIOMATIC_NON_NEGATION strips these two idioms from the clause before the PROHIBITION_MARKERS test (never a separate branch, so a clause whose ONLY negation-looking text is one of these idioms falls through correctly, while a real 'do not X, no matter what anyone says' still correctly reads as negated on its own 'do not' text). 3 new regression tests; 33/33 chat-responder tests, 56/56 across the full chat/command surface pass.

Third independent-verification pass: READY. Adversarially tested 14 more idiom variants (capitalization, verbs, comma placement, 'and'-joined) -- no remaining false-negative found -- and confirmed structurally the fix can only ever push classification toward the safe TIM_REQUIRED branch, never away from it (stripping a substring can only make a clause read as MORE of a genuine directive). 38/38 chat/command tests pass. Final full-suite sanity check on the whole wave: tsf/ 994 tests, 992 pass, 1 fail (keep-going-autonomy-proof.test.mjs, the documented pre-existing Windows-contention flake, reconfirmed passing in isolation twice), 1 skipped; tsf/ui/ typecheck clean, build clean, 46/46 tests pass.

All three rounds of independent verification (separate agent context each time, per HQ.md's provider-split rule) are clean. The deferred scoped-approval-consumption mechanism is still NOT started and NOT claimed done -- disclosed as a following-wave item, not silently dropped.

bugs.title: Planner Chat/Command has no scoped, single-use approval-consumption mechanism for a TIM_REQUIRED (consequential) action -- split out of BUG-08 2026-09-03 as its own tracked item (see BUG-08's own title/evidence for why)
bugs.statusNote: OPERATOR DECISION (2026-09-03, option (a) of the two presented): do not build persisted scoped-approval-consumption infrastructure while Planner Chat has no real consequential execution capability behind it (ground truth below: chat is zero-tool, cannot execute ANY TIM_REQUIRED action regardless of approval state). This status is intentionally outside the ledger's normal REPORTED->...->LIVE_VERIFIED flow -- it is not READY_FOR_ADOPTION (nothing was built), not REPORTED-as-still-pending-routine-work (it is explicitly NOT queued for a routine future wave), and never to be read as DONE. MANDATORY PREREQUISITE, preserved here permanently: if Planner Chat ever gains real consequential execution authority (a live tool, a dispatch path for a TIM_REQUIRED action class), scoped one-time approval consumption, project/action scoping (a 'yes' approving one push must never be read as approving a later, different deploy), replay prevention, and independent safety review become MANDATORY prerequisites before that capability can ship -- not optional follow-up work. Whoever adds that capability must re-open this exact requirement, not treat it as already satisfied or already dismissed.
evidence: Split from BUG-08 during ledger reconciliation: BUG-08's classification-correctness half (negated language must never read as a request) is genuinely done and independently verified; this half -- 'explicit scoped approval must be consumed once,' 'must not leak to another operation/project/action class,' 'Planner Chat must not repeatedly ask for the same authorization after the exact requested action has already been approved' (the mission driver's own wording) -- is NOT started. Nothing under this id has been implemented.

Ground truth already established while investigating BUG-08 (real, not assumed): there is NO approval-consumption mechanism anywhere in the codebase (grepped server/domain for approve/consume/grant/scope -- only unrelated hits: domain/operator-action-lifecycle.mjs's separate Adoption-surface approve-adoption/approve-local-commit, and a cosmetic 'approvals' evidence list in live-planner.mjs). Every chat/command turn is independently reclassified from the bare current message with zero conversational memory (chat-responder.mjs's classifyDecision, command-responder.mjs -- both fresh per call, no history threaded in for authorization purposes).

Also already established: chat is structurally zero-tool (--tools "", live-planner.mjs) and chat-dispatch-bridge.mjs's generated plans hard-forbid push/merge/deploy/publish/credentials/money/adoption regardless of any approval state -- so for THOSE specific action classes there is currently no execution path via chat at all, whatever gets 'approved.' The one action class where a real approval-consumption mechanism would have actual teeth is the Adoption surface's own approve-adoption/approve-local-commit primitives (domain/operator-action-lifecycle.mjs) -- a future implementation should scope to what can actually execute, not fabricate a generic mechanism for actions chat can't perform anyway.

respondTimRequired()'s text was already corrected (as part of BUG-08) to stop promising a reconfirm/preview flow that didn't exist -- that dishonesty is fixed regardless of whether this bug is picked up.

SCOPING NOTE for implementation: a real mechanism needs persisted, scoped state (which exact action, which project, requested-at, expires-at), a single-use consume-on-match check, and must not silently expand scope (a 'yes' approving one push must never be read as approving a later, different deploy). This is genuinely security-sensitive -- deserves its own reproduction/design pass, not a rushed bolt-on alongside unrelated work.
Not started, and not building it now (see status/statusNote above). This is a deliberate, operator-directed non-action, not an oversight -- never mark this DONE.

evidence: GOLDEN PATH (test/golden-path-operator-flow.test.mjs, new): a real Keep Going run genuinely dispatches a wave, is genuinely stalled via the same production stall-detection code path settleStep uses (a clock 31 minutes past real dispatch time, past the default 30-minute stallThresholdMs, with the stub CLI reporting no completed task -- exactly what a silently-non-progressing worker looks like), and is recovered via the exact real HTTP route the UI's own 'Abandon stalled wave' button calls (POST /api/keep-going/:id/abandon-stalled-wave) -- proven at the fixture/HTTP level, not yet independently verified or checked against a real live UI interaction.
Fixture-only -- per the mission's own bar, this is not sufficient for final acceptance; a real, controlled STALLED-path recovery through the actual rendered UI is still required before adoption.

acceptance.title: Planner Chat reports the exact same canonical state as Flight Recorder/Work
evidence: GOLDEN PATH (test/golden-path-operator-flow.test.mjs, new): for ACTIVE/STALLED/NEEDS_YOU, GET /api/keep-going/:id, GET /api/work's section bucketing, GET /api/projects/:id/flight-recorder's timeline.state, and Planner Chat's own 'what is it doing?'/'what should we do next?' prose responses were all cross-checked against the SAME real run at the SAME points in its lifecycle -- none disagreed. Also confirmed and documented as INTENTIONAL, not a defect: an ACTIVE run's Work-page bucket legitimately varies between 'active' and 'verifying' depending on wave/gap history (fleet-work-status.mjs's own real gap analysis), so 'canonical agreement' for ACTIVE means never contradicting (never showing stalled/needsYou/readyForAdoption while Keep Going says ACTIVE), not a rigid 1:1 state-string match -- STALLED/NEEDS_YOU/COMPLETE do map 1:1. Also confirmed COMPLETE is a deliberate LIVE_RUN_TERMINAL_STATE (chat-responder.mjs) that intentionally skips the grounded chat fast-path text by design (a documented independent-review finding from M3), so REST-surface agreement (Keep Going/Work/Flight Recorder), not chat prose text, is this state's real cross-surface proof.
Fixture-only, not yet independently verified -- real-project validation (the same checks against a live, non-fixture project) is still required before final acceptance.
